comments.text:
Who are the indigenous people of Saba and what are features???

Could someone answer that please?

replies.author: @dmck6422
replies.text: ​​@ImpossibleTravel38Hi thx for the information. It's quite fascinating that most ABORIGINAL indigenous people always seem to vanish into thin air when Europeans arrive. The pen sure is a powerful weapon. Very interesting!

replies.author: @ImpossibleTravel38
replies.text:
I can explain it like this. Long before Europeans ever laid eyes on the tiny volcanic island of Saba, three completely different groups of indigenous people called it home over thousands of years, and each group brought its own unique vibe to the island.
It all started more than three thousand years ago with a nomadic group of hunter-gatherers called the Ciboney. They lived a very simple, on-the-go lifestyle along the coast, mostly setting up temporary shelters, fishing, and making tools out of shells since they didn't even know how to make pottery yet. Centuries later, a much more settled group of advanced farmers called the Arawaks arrived from South America. These were the people who actually named the island "Siba," which literally means "the rock" and is where the name Saba comes from. The Arawaks weren't just moving through; they built permanent inland villages, farmed crops like sweet potatoes and cassava, and even used the island's natural caves for their spiritual rituals. Right before Europeans arrived, a fierce, mobile warrior culture called the Caribs moved in. They were legendary navigators who sailed the Caribbean in massive seagoing canoes and were known for their strong, dominant nature.
The coolest part about Saba's history is that even though the island is incredibly small, it acted like a bustling trade hub. Archaeologists have dug up things like flint from Antigua and beautiful pottery from other faraway islands, which proves these indigenous groups were constantly trading and networking with their neighbors. Sadly, by the 1600s, when European powers started fighting over the island, the original indigenous people completely vanished due to colonial wars and diseases.
